title: Professional Sass Code Review knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which mental model best explains “Professional Sass Code Review” in Dart Sass?
options: The browser executes Sass source directly, so a compilation step is unnecessary.
Readable SCSS guarantees correct browser rendering, accessibility, and performance without output review.
The best solution is always to replace native CSS behavior with a new Sass abstraction.

The design problem is usually consistency across many related styles, not the ability to write shorter syntax. Combine semantic tokens, a clear module boundary, reusable component patterns, and CSS-native runtime features where each has a distinct role.
questions.answer_key: The design problem is usually consistency across many related styles, not the ability to write shorter syntax. Combine semantic tokens, a clear module boundary, reusable component patterns, and CSS-native runtime features where each has a distinct role.
questions.explanation: The design problem is usually consistency across many related styles, not the ability to write shorter syntax. Combine semantic tokens, a clear module boundary, reusable component patterns, and CSS-native runtime features where each has a distinct role. The alternative choices confuse Sass compilation with browser execution or claim guarantees that require independent tests.

questions.prompt: When applying “Reviewing naming and organization”, which approach is the most reliable?
options: Prefer deeply nested selectors because fewer source lines always mean simpler and safer CSS.
Silence every warning before determining whether it identifies a deprecated or incorrect construct.
For reviewing naming and organization, identify the relevant source rule, predict the intended result, and check the emitted CSS against that expectation.
Skip compilation and infer the final selector list and property values from the source file alone.
questions.answer_key: For reviewing naming and organization, identify the relevant source rule, predict the intended result, and check the emitted CSS against that expectation.
questions.explanation: For reviewing naming and organization, identify the relevant source rule, predict the intended result, and check the emitted CSS against that expectation. Compare the compiled output with the stated intent and preserve browser-native behavior where it is required.

questions.prompt: Which review decision most directly supports maintainability for “Professional Sass Code Review”?
options: Expose internal implementation details as public API and postpone documentation until after release.
Design the public interface for the next developer: document tokens and arguments, keep internals private, compile from a documented entrypoint, and demonstrate the result in a small consumer page.
Generate every possible selector or theme combination, even when most variants are never used.
Treat successful compilation as proof that the interface is accessible and behaves correctly in every browser.
questions.answer_key: Design the public interface for the next developer: document tokens and arguments, keep internals private, compile from a documented entrypoint, and demonstrate the result in a small consumer page.
questions.explanation: Design the public interface for the next developer: document tokens and arguments, keep internals private, compile from a documented entrypoint, and demonstrate the result in a small consumer page. The other choices increase output, assume unverified behavior, or make the public interface harder to maintain.
